answer: Because the zenith index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the pearl audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a sonnet index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Filling 98 aliases therefore needs 98 distinct prompts, so the operator forfeits the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
